Commentary.Commentary: Everything till now has gone the Windies' way. The ploy to open the bowling with Nurse turned out to be a masterstroke. Their pacers also did their job well. Especially, Williams who finished with career-best figures. Paul also impressed, and Russell too bowled with a lot of steam. Badree though had a day to forget as he took a pounding from the Bangladesh batters. Overall, Brathwaite will be quite happy with how the game stands now and he will expect his batsmen to chase this down. Will they do so or will the visitors' bowlers come to the fore? Join us in the second innings to find out.

Bangladesh do manage to play out their twenty overs but it has not been a batting scorecard to look back at. After being inserted, they got off to worst of starts by losing both their openers for golden ducks in the first over. Shakib then was dropped in the next over but he too could not make most of the life as he and Das fell on consecutive balls, which meant Bangladesh were 4 down in the Powerplay. Rahim then along with Mahmudullah counter-attacked and the two added a quickfire 47-run stand. But once the former fell, the procession continued and the visitors finished with a total which is below par.
A single! So no boundary from the last over and only 4 from it. Carlos bowls another yorker. Rahman jams it out towards point for a run. BANGLADESH END WITH 143!
A bumper outside off, Rahman goes for the pull but misses it by a week. No boundaries in the last over as of now. One ball to go.
Slower ball on off, Hossain does well to wait for it and then slap it through covers for a run.
Good length outside off, the batsman swings and misses.
A full toss outside off, Rahman slaps it through covers for a run.
A yorker to begin with. The batsman fails to dig it out and gets hit on the boot. The players appeal but the umpire stays put. Missing leg again. Leg bye taken by the batsmen.
Carlos Brathwaite to bowl the last over.
No fifer for Williams but end of an exceptional spell. A single through mid-wicket to end his fourth over. 4-0-28-4 is what his figures reads.
Only one more delivery left now as Rahman works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Good length on off, kept out. 2 more to get a fifer.
Mustafizur Rahman is the new man in.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! 4-fer for Williams and he is not finished yet. A short ball following the batsman as he makes room. Islam tries to defend but the ball kisses the outside edge and settles into the gloves of the keeper.
FOUR! Streaky but very handy for Bangladesh. On a length around off, slanting away from the batsman. Islam tries to defend but gets an outside edge and the ball races to the third man fence.
Another slower ball outside off, Islam misses. The umpire calls it a wide.
Rubel Hossain walks out to the middle.

OUT! Hasan holes out and the end is nigh for Bangladesh. Williams gets his third and once again, it is the slower ball which works to great effect. An off cutter on middle, Mehidy swings but only manages to get a top edge. The ball balloons towards Nurse at mid-wicket who runs in and takes a neat catch.
Eases it down to long on for a run.
A yorker on the pads, Hasan misses the flick and gets hit on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Going down leg.

Fuller outside off, Islam drives it towards point. The fielder there dives to his right, picks it cleanly and then gets rid of it quickly. However, his shy at the non-striker's end misses and the batsmen complete a run.
Another swing and another miss. Slower ball outside off, Islam dances down the track and goes for the heave but does not connect.
Short and outside off, Islam tries to upper cut but does not connect.
Good length outside off, Islam tries to put bat on ball but misses.
Back of a length on off, Islam guides it down to third man to keep strike.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
On middle, tucked around the corner with soft hands and the batsmen run two.
Guided down to third man for a run.
Another slower ball on off, it pitches and then moves away. Islam pokes at it and gets beaten.
Nazmul Islam is the new man in.

OUT! BOWLED 'EM! What a brilliant delivery by Williams! He has completely foxed Mahmudullah there. He comes running in and then delivers a slower delivery on a fuller length. Mahmudullah comes down the track but does not pick it. He is way too early into the stroke and the ball goes under his bat uprooting the off pole. Mahmudullah perishes after getting a start and Bangladesh are in a real danger to get bowled out.
Yorker. Dug to covers for nothing.

Tremendous stuff from Fletcher. He saves a run for his team once again. Mahmudullah tucks the length ball to mid-wicket and calls for two. The fielder runs in from deep and throws the ball back in quickly to stop the batsmen in their stride.
Gets it to deep backward square leg off the inner half of the bat for another run.
Similar length on the pads, flicked through square leg. One run taken.
On a length around off, Hasan gets an edge on it to third man and changes strike.
A fuller ball outside off, driven to covers.
On the stumps on off, Mahmdullah keeps it out.
Shortish in length on off, Hasan tries to pull but gets a top edge which lands well short of the man at fine leg. A single taken.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
FOUR! Just over! A low full toss on the middle pole. Hasan flicks it over short mid-wicket and a boundary results.
Fuller on middle, Hasan tries to drive it but gets an inside edge towards mid-wicket.
Mehidy Hasan is the new man in.

OUT! Ariful Haque has been given the marching orders as he was cleaned up by Russell. This has landed on a length around off, Ariful tries to flick but it brushes his pads and then goes towards the keeper. He picks the ball up and then scores a direct hit at the non-striker's end to find Mahmudullah short. The umpire raises his finger but then asks Mahmudullah to wait as he sees the bail at the other end is out of its groove. They now go upstairs to check what exactly happened and replays show that the ball has clipped the bail before going into the mitts of the Ramdin. Ariful starts walking back and probably takes Bangladesh's hopes of reaching a good score along with him.

Now then! What has happened here? Mahmudullah has been run out at the bowler's end but has Ariful been bowled before that? They are going upstairs to check. One thing though is for sure, one of the batsmen has to walk back.
Andre Russell is back on.
Full outside off, Mahmudullah guides it to point.
On a length around middle, worked down to long on for a run.
Good length closer to the off pole. Haque tries to guide it but gets beaten.
WIDE! Outside off, Haque flashes at it and gets beaten.
The batsman drives this through the covers. One run added to the total.
Lovely bowling! Excellent comeback! A yorker on middle, Ariful tries to jam it out but gets an inside edge down to third man for a run.
FOUR! Top shot! Slightly short on middle, Haque picks the length up early and he pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Keemo Paul is back into the attack.
Yes, he can! A dot to end. Just a run from the over. Another length ball outside off, Mahmudullah, just like his partner tries to cut but misses.
A single! Just 1 from the first 5 balls as Haque guides it towards point where Lewis makes a good stop diving to his left. Can he now finish the over well?
Four dots in a row! Another length ball outside off, the batsman fails to cut it.
Shortish again outside off, the batsman slashes but does not connect.
Two dots to start! Length ball on off, Das drives it towards point.
Slightly short outside off, the batsman tries to cut but misses.
Carlos Brathwaite is back on.
Goes fuller this time on off, Ariful drives it towards wide mid off and takes a run.
Another length ball outside off and another single as it is played down towards third man.
Goes wide of the crease and bowls it on a length around off, Haque chops it towards point and gets to the other end.
Back of a length on off, Haque pushes it past the diving fielder at point and runs two.
Another short ball on off, Mahmudullah guides it down to third man for another single.
Shortish on off, Ariful guides it down to third man for a run.
Short, pulled to deep backward square leg for another easy single.
On a length on the pads, tucked to the on side. Fourth single off the over.
Defended off the back foot by Mahmudullah.
Short ball in line of the stumps, worked to the fine leg region. One run results.
Full toss on the pads, flicked to square leg for another single.
Starts his second spell with a back of a length ball on middle, driven down the ground for a run.
Andre Russell is back on.
Slower ball outside off, Mahmudullah tries to cut but gets beaten.
FOUR! Another gift! Down the leg side, Mahmudullah tickles it fine and fetches another boundary. He moves onto 28.

NOT OUT! Missing leg and Windies lose their sole review. Was a poor one to be honest. Williams bowls it on middle and then angles it into the batsman. Haque tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The Windies players appeal as the ball rolls towards square leg and the batsmen run a leg bye. The umpire shakes his head. Williams really likes it and he convinces his skipper to take it upstairs. Replays roll in and they show the ball to be going down with the angle.
Review time! An appeal for an LBW has been turned down. Ariful Haque is the man in question. Looks to be missing the leg stump.
Ariful Haque is next.

OUT! Timely breakthrough and Bangladesh now have half their side back in the hut. Poor shot by Rahim. The third man was moved in a bit finer and he has fallen for the trap. Williams bangs it in short on off, Rahim arches his back and tries to play the upper cut. Does not generate a lot of power in the shot and it goes straight into the hands of Powell in that region. A promising stand has been cut short and Windies now will look to get things back in their control.
FOUR! Brilliant by Rahim! He makes room and he gets a short ball outside off. Rahim guides it very fine on the off side and a boundary results.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Kesrick Williams is on.

FOUR! A boundary to finish another expensive over. 13 from it. Good innovation from Rahim. He moves across and plays the paddle scoop over the keeper and into the boundary. Yes, wickets have fallen but the visitors continue their attacking approach and it is paying off for them.
An action replay of the last delivery. Two dots in a row.
Shortish outside off, Rahim goes for a cut but does not connect.
Fullish on off, Rahim hits it through covers and the batsmen run two.
Length on off, guided down to third man for a run.

FIVE WIDES! Poor ball by the Windies skipper, down the leg side, Mahmudullah misses the flick. The keeper too fails to collect it and the ball races away. Brathwaite is not happy with it being called a wide and rightly so. Snicko later on shows a spike as the ball passes the bat.
Fuller on middle, worked down to long on for a run.
Carlos Brathwaite is into the attack.

SIX! Stand and deliver! That has been hit with authority. Length ball around off, Mahmudullah makes room and just lofts it over the long off fence. Ends the over with a bang. 12 from this one and 29 from the last 2.
The batsman opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man.
A slower bouncer this time but it bounces way above the batsman's head. Wide signaled.
Extra bounce on this one! Paul bends his back on this one and bowls it on a back of a length. Rahim tries to fend it but the ball goes off the gloves down to third man for a run.
Smart batting! They got a big  last over and now are looking to rotate strike as Mahmudullah guides this down to third man for a run.
Slower ball but the bowler misses his radar. It is down the leg side, wided.
Back of a length on middle, Mahmudullah tucks it to mid-wicket.
Rahim makes room and hits it hard towards mid off who makes a good stop diving to his left. A single taken.
WIDE! Down the leg side, Rahim misses the flick and a wide is signaled.

SIX! Bang! What. A. Shot. Mahmudullah is a powerful man and he is showing it here in St. Kitts. A flighted ball on off from Badree, the batsman just powers it over long on fence nonchalantly for a maximum. 17 runs off Badree's third. He has been taken to cleaners this evening.
FOUR! Punishment day it is for Samuel Badree. He bowls a fuller ball on leg and Mahmudullah drives it powerfully to the long on fence. Two off two for Mahmudullah.

FOUR! Normally Badree is quite straight but today he is erring in his line and Bangladesh batsmen are making him pay. Shorter outside off, guided through third man for a boundary. A boundary after three singles.
Slower this time around off, pushed through cover-point. One run taken.
On the pads, worked to the on side for another run.
Flighted on off, pushed to long on for a run.
Back of a length on off, kept out. A dot to end the Powerplay, a dreadful one for Bangladesh. They are 43 for 4 after 6.
Works it with the angle towards mid-wicket.
Mahmudullah does well to negotiate the hat-trick ball out. A good delivery, attacking the stumps and on a length. Mahmudullah keeps it out.
Mahmudullah makes his way out to the middle. He will be facing the hat-trick ball.

OUT! He has taken it cleanly! The dropped catch has not cost a lot. Marlon Samuels can now breathe a sigh of relief. Brilliant by Williams. Once again the short ball does the trick. This time it is outside off, Shakib plays the upper cut. He does connect well but Williams there holds onto the ball but then realizes that he is losing his balance. He shows good awareness by throwing the ball up in the air, crosses the fence, then comes back in and catches it. The umpire goes upstairs to check whether it is cleanly taken, and the replays show it is clean as a whistle. Once again, Bangladesh lose two in an over and now are in dire straits. Hat-trick ball coming up.
Has Williams pulled of a blinder? Well he is pretty confident about it as the umpires go upstairs to check. OUT is the soft signal. Shakib is the man in question. A huge moment in the game.
Mushfiqur Rahim is the new man in.

OUT! In the air... taken! The Powerplay keeps getting better for the Windies as Keemo Paul strikes in his first over. The short ball does the trick. Unlike the last delivery, this time he gets it to bounce a lot more as he bowls it a touch shorter. Das goes for the pull but gets a top edge which goes high up in the air towards backward square leg. Fletcher there settles himself under it and takes it. Third down for Bangladesh and not many teams win a game after losing three in the Powerplay.

Another brilliant effort in the field by Fletcher. On the shorter side again, not that short though. Das picks the length up early and pulls it towards deep mid-wicket. Fletcher there runs to his left, and does really well to push it back into play with one hand. The batsmen run two.
Keemo Paul replaces Andre Russell.
Whips this through mid-wicket and Das retains strike. 9 from Samuel's second and he has gone for 18 in his two. You don't normally see the leggie go for a lot.

Lovely fielding! Das steps down the track and chips the ball over mid off. He might have felt that he has hit it for a certain boundary. But the fielder at long on, runs to his left, dives and saves two for his side.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Quicker and on the shorter side, Hasan guides it to point.
FOUR! Crashed! Badree pays the price of bowling a little too full as Shakib hits him hard through the covers. He finds the gap and a boundary results. Runs starting to come thick and fast now.
Flatter on the stumps, Das pushes it towards wide mid on for a run.

FOUR! Make that three! 15 from Russell's second. Another half-tracker and width on offer outside off, Hasan says thank you so much and guides it over point as the ball races away. Bangladesh needed this big over, this should get them going nicely.

FOUR! Not off the middle but Shakib will take it. A good follow-up delivery by Russell, a bumper, aimed at the body of the batsman. Shakib goes for the pull but the ball takes the top edge and races to the fine leg fence. Second boundary in the over.
A corker of a yorker there. Had it only been on the stumps. Shakib again is beaten in pace as he tries to jam it out.
FOUR! Who will these runs hurt the most? Marlon Samuels. A short ball outside off, Shakib loves it there. He cuts it over backward point and gets a boundary. His first.

Up and over! Not a boundary but three handy runs! Shorter in length on middle, Das picks the length up early. He pulls it over the mid-wicket fielder. The timing is not all that great but still enough to fetch three.
Clever delivery! He bowled the last over at very good pace and this time delivers a slower ball on off. Das taps it towards point. He wants a run but is sent back by his partner correctly.
Fuller on middle, driven to mid on for a run. 9 off Badree's first over.
Gets behind this one nicely and keeps it out off the front foot.
FOUR! Shot! Das is looking to up the ante and Badree is proving to be expensive in his first over. A touch shorter outside off, Das cuts it through cover-point and gets another boundary.
FOUR! Innovation from Das. He slips but has struck it nicely. A flighted ball on middle and off, Das slogs it over square leg and earns a boundary.
Faster one on middle, Das comes forward and away to keep it out to the off side.
Liton has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Samuel Badree is into the attack. Surprising, especially after a double-wicket over by Nurse.
A single to end another good over for the Windies. A good bouncer, a well-directed one. Das tucks it around the corner and gets to the other end.
BEATEN AGAIN! Russell is proving too hot to handle for Das. He bowls this full and outside off, the sucker ball. Liton goes for a booming drive but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Short outside off, the ball has a lot of fizz on it. Das once again is beaten by pace as he goes for the pull.
Goes very full on the pads, Das is late on the flick shot. He misses to get hit on the pads.
On a length and at a good pace. The batsman defends it.

DROPPED! Who is the culprit? Marlon Samuels. A sitter, that is what you can call that. But the question here is, what is Shakib doing? Your team has lost two wickets in the first over, you should be a touch cautious but no. He goes for a flashy drive to a ball which is on a length. It goes uppishly towards Samuels at short covers who gets two hands to it but spills it. A reprieve for the Bangladesh skipper, can he make them pay? The visitors would hope he can.
Andre Russell to bowl from the other end.
On the stumps and kept out. End of a double-wicket over. Brilliant by Nurse, a captain could not have asked for anything more after winning the toss and opting to field.

Fuller on middle, Hasan pushes it towards mid off for a quick run. The fielder there failed to pick it up cleanly, had he done it, there could have been a chance of a run out at the non-striker's end.
Shakib Al Hasan, the skipper strides out to the middle. He needs to play a captain's knock here.

OUT! TIMBER! Ashley Nurse, what a first over this is turning out to be. He opened the bowling as there were two left-handers and he has got both of them. Sarkar too bags a golden duck. Poor from him. He goes back to a fuller length delivery and that proves to be his undoing. The ball skids through and even before he gets his bat down, the ball hits timber. He stands there in disbelief and then starts trudging back. Another failure for Sarkar and Bangladesh have both their openers back in the hut in the first over itself.
Again fires it on the stumps, Das pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a run.

FOUR! A wicket on the first ball and a boundary on the second. Liton Das gets off the mark in style. Flatter and outside off, Das waits for the ball to come to him and then guides it through short third man for a boundary. First of the game.
Liton Das is the new man in.

OUT! And guess what? He strikes on the very first ball. The move to begin with the offie has paid dividends. What a start for the Windies, they are ecstatic as they have got the big fish. Tamim walks back without troubling the scorers. He tries to take on the bowler first up by dancing down the track. He though comes down a touch early and seeing that, Nurse bowls it shorter and outside off. Tamim tries to cut but misses and the keeper does the rest.

We are all set for the game to begin now. Out come the umpires and they are followed by the Windies players. Tamim Iqbal and Soumya Sarkar are the openers for Bangladesh. The former will be on strike and he will be facing Ashley Nurse. We normally see Samuel Badree open the bowling for the Windies but due to two left-handers, it is Nurse who will bowl the first over.
Good news! It was a passing shower and the covers are being removed. Action to resume shortly.

Bad news! We were moments away from the start of the game but the heavens opened up. It is pouring down at the moment and the groundsmen rush out with the covers. Let us hope it is just a passing shower and action resumes as soon as possible. Fingers crossed.
Bangladesh (XI) - Tamim Iqbal, Soumya Sarkar, Liton Das, Mushfiqur Rahim(w), Shakib Al Hasan(c), Mahmudullah, Ariful Haque, Mehidy Hasan, Mustafizur Rahman, Nazmul Islam, Rubel Hossain.
Windies (XI) - Evin Lewis, Andre Fletcher, Marlon Samuels, Rovman Powell, Denesh Ramdin(w), Carlos Brathwaite(c), Andre Russell, Ashley Nurse, Samuel Badree, Keemo Paul, Kesrick Williams.
Toss - Windies win the toss and elect to field.

Test series - won by the Windies. ODI series - won by Bangladesh. Now it is time for the shortest version of the game. A format in which the hosts are a force to reckon with. They are surely favourites heading into the 1st T20I but the visitors have momentum on their side. Can they carry forward the momentum and hold the edge heading into the second game or will the home side justify their tag of World Champions? Stay tuned to find out.
